# Dock preview vnode arrives under a generated id; createDeltas refuses

## Context

Two of the five-beat journey's scenes are red at `dev@db3de7d7b5`, and they were green at the `#17844` census head `03219a75b7` four days ago:

```
[chromium] › WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:2548 › scene 4 — reintegration: whole stack home, commit precedes the vessel self-close
[chromium] › WorkstationFiveBeatNL.spec.mjs:2767 › scene 5 — the signature: full journey in ONE run, two-take beat-log equality
  2 failed · 8 passed · 3 skipped
```

Both fail in the same place — `fixtures.mjs:138`, *"no worker error reached the page console, and the page threw nothing"* — the `workerErrors` gate @neo-opus-ada shipped in `#18554` / PR `#18716`. The two errors it catches:

```
VDom Worker: Error: createDeltas() must be called for the same node.
  new: {id: neo-vnode-806, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}, old: {id: neo-dock-preview-2, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}

App Worker: Error: worker.Base#promiseMessage: no live port for destination "<uuid>"
  (remoteMethod Neo.main.DomAccess.setBodyCls) — a window closed?
```

Reproduced 2/2 at head, headless, `--workers=1`, with `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` wired. The showcase beat that `#17844`'s census carried as this file's one red is **green** now — `#18770` repaired it — so this file's red count did not change while its reason did.

Environment control: the same Brain runtime revision drove both the red head and the green control, so the runtime pin is not the variable.

## The Problem

`git bisect run` over the 140 commits between the census head and `dev`, keyed on the presence of the `createDeltas` line rather than on exit code (the showcase beat is separately red at old heads), names:

```
baed5db7ae1df873f9137616e93d929b871df192 is the first bad commit
test(e2e): a worker or page error nobody named fails its test ... (#18554) (#18716)
```

**That commit is the gate, not the defect** — and the distinction is the whole point of this ticket. Per-head evidence:

| head | `createDeltas` lines | any `* Worker: Error` line | scenes 4/5 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `67b517dd32`, `d6d0d14bd4`, `46a52c8fd0` (pre-gate) | 0 | **0** | pass |
| `baed5db7ae` (the gate) and every head after | 3 | 3–4 | fail |

Zero worker-error lines of **any** kind at the pre-gate heads is the tell. `#18554`'s own commit message says the mirror "forwarded `console.error` and `onerror` only"; the gate commit is what made worker errors reach the page console at all. So the instrument could not see this class of error before it landed — **absence in the pre-gate logs is a property of the instrument, not evidence that the errors were not firing.**

What the evidence does settle: the `createDeltas` guard is old — `git log -S "must be called for the same node"` dates it to `8b78c30743`, and `baed5db7ae` does not touch it. A commit that added an observation surface and did not touch the guard is a weak candidate for having caused what the guard reports.

So the open question is **not** "which commit broke this" but "is this vnode identity discontinuity a live defect or long-standing noise the journey always produced". It is answered by looking at the mechanism, not by more bisecting.

## The Architectural Reality

- `createDeltas` refuses because the two nodes disagree on `id` while agreeing on `cId`: the new node carries an auto-generated `neo-vnode-806`, the old one the component-derived `neo-dock-preview-2`. A component whose vdom carries an explicit `id` produced a vnode that did not.
- `cId` agreeing is what makes this narrow: the delta engine is looking at the same component across a re-render, and only the node id moved.
- The second error is a different class: `worker.Base#promiseMessage` resolving a `Neo.main.DomAccess.setBodyCls` against a port whose window has closed. Scene 4 is *"whole stack home, commit precedes the vessel self-close"* — a remote call racing a deliberate window close is exactly this journey's subject, so the guess that it is a teardown-ordering artefact is plausible and unverified.
- Both errors are currently **unnamed**: `workerErrors.expect(RegExp)` exists precisely so a test can declare an error it means to provoke. Neither scene declares either one, which is why the gate fails them.

## The Fix

1. Read the dock preview's vdom at the moment of the refused delta — `neo-dock-preview-2`'s `id` — and establish whether the generated-id node is a real identity break or a node the engine legitimately re-keys.
2. If it is a break, repair it where the id is lost. `src/util/VNode.mjs` and `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs` are the surfaces `baed5db7ae` touched in the same window and are the first places to rule in or out.
3. Settle the `setBodyCls` port race on its own terms; if it is a legitimate teardown artefact the scene should **name** it via `workerErrors.expect(...)` rather than the gate being loosened.
4. Whichever way each resolves, scenes 4 and 5 end green without weakening the gate.

## Decision Record impact

`none`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The `createDeltas` refusal for `neo-dock-preview-2` is characterised: the vdom that produced the generated-id node is read at the failing render, and the ticket records whether it is an identity break or a legitimate re-key. — **MET**, [comment](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18998#issuecomment-5744920125): the throw is the CHILD recursion at `Helper.mjs:323`, not the top-level pairing; Case 2 matches on `componentId` alone while the guard requires id equality, and the pair is the Preview's expanded root against an unexpanded node of the same component — an asymmetric expansion, which the loop's own comment says the `VdomLifecycle` mixin prevents.
- [ ] If it is a break, it is repaired at the surface that loses the id, with a red-first arm that fails on the unrepaired engine.
- [ ] No `createDeltas` refusal remains in `WorkstationFiveBeatNL` at a named `dev` head, `--workers=1`, Brain runtime wired, at `--repeat-each=3`.
- [ ] `#17844`'s census row for this file is updated from this outcome.

- **Reading the bisect as attribution.** The first bad commit added the observation surface. Filing this as "`#18716` regressed the dock preview" would have sent the next reader into a gate diff that cannot contain the answer.
- **Reading pre-gate silence as health.** Zero worker-error lines at the good heads is what a mirror that does not forward them looks like.
- **Keying the bisect on exit code.** The showcase beat is independently red before `#18770`, so an exit-code predicate would have found that instead. The predicate grepped for the `createDeltas` line.
- **Running a single `--grep`'d arm.** `-g "scene 4"` alone passes at head; the failure needs its predecessors in-file — `#17844`'s trap 3.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-19T19:22:04Z

## Source read at `dev@db3de7d7b5` — where the generated id comes from, and the two candidates it leaves

Recorded before the live read, so the next pass starts from evidence rather than from this ticket's opening sentence.

**The generated id has a source.** [`Preview#getAffordanceVdom`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.mjs) returns a node carrying `cls`, `data-dock-target` and `style` — **and no `id`**. It is the only child the overlay ever mounts: [`afterSetDockPreview`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/dashboard/dock/interaction/Preview.mjs#L284) sets `me.vdom.cn = affordance ? [me.getAffordanceVdom(affordance)] : []` and updates. So the affordance child is re-BUILT on every preview change and takes a fresh `neo-vnode-*` each time.

Both refusals in the run agree on that, and they are the two distinct pairs across the whole log:

```
new: {id: neo-vnode-806, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}, old: {id: neo-dock-preview-2, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}
new: {id: neo-vnode-832, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}, old: {id: neo-dock-preview-2, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}
```

Two different generated ids, one component, and in both the OLD side is the component's own root while the NEW side is a generated node. `cId` agrees throughout, so the delta engine has the right component and the wrong node.

**That narrows it to two candidates, and the difference decides the fix.**

1. **The new tree is rooted one level too deep** — `createDeltas` receives the affordance child as the new root and the component root as the old one. Then the id instability is a symptom and the repair is in the update path, not in `Preview`.
2. **The component root lost its own `id` in the new tree** and was re-keyed as `neo-vnode-*`, so the ids in the message are root-vs-root after all. Then the repair is wherever the root is rebuilt.

Nothing in `Preview` replaces `me.vdom` wholesale — `afterSetDockPreview` mutates `cn` and `applyTargetGeometry` mutates `cn[0].style` — so neither candidate is settled by reading this class, which is why this is a note and not an AC tick.

**The probe that separates them** is AC-1 as written: read the component's vdom AND the vnode handed to `createDeltas` at the failing render, rather than at boot. `neo-vnode-806` appears in scene 4 and `neo-vnode-832` in scene 5, so either scene reproduces it.

**Not yet touched:** whether a stable id on the affordance child (`${me.id}__affordance`) would fix candidate 1 — under candidate 1 it would only mask the level error, which is exactly the reason to measure before changing anything.

Head, both runs: `dev@db3de7d7b5`, headless, `--workers=1`, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` wired. 2/2 reproduced.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-19T19:30:22Z

## The throwing call site is one of two, and that reframes the two candidates in `Helper`'s terms

Follow-up to the note above — still source-reading, still no live probe, and it narrows further than I expected.

The guard is [`Helper#createDeltas`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/vdom/Helper.mjs#L279) and it is the only site that can raise this message. Four call sites reach it, and two are eliminated by the message's own shape — `cId` EQUAL, `id` DIFFERENT:

| call site | pairing | can it produce id-differs? |
|---|---|---|
| `#L720` moved-node loop | `oldVnode: oldVnodeMap.get(id).vnode` against the new node **of that same id** | **No** — the old node is fetched BY the id being compared |
| `#L323` child recursion | positional child pairing inside an id-guarded loop | unlikely; children here are the affordance node, not the root |
| `#L787` moved-node insert | `oldVnode: movedNode.vnode` against a `vnode` resolved separately | **Yes** |
| `#L850` `update()` entry | `oldVnode: opts.vnode` (last rendered) against `vnode = createVnode(opts.vdom)` | **Yes** |

So the two candidates from the previous note become two named call sites, and each says something different about the defect:

- **`update()` at `#L850`.** `vnode = me.createVnode(opts.vdom)`, so a new root with a generated id means **the `vdom` object handed to this update carried no `id`** while the last rendered vnode carried `neo-dock-preview-2`. That is a component whose vdom root lost its identity between renders — the repair would be wherever that id is dropped, and it would be a general defect, not a dock one.
- **`#L787`, the moved-node insert.** The overlay is mounted and unmounted against the dock during a drag, so a genuine node move is in play here in a way it is not for most components. If this is the site, the pairing itself is wrong and the ids are a symptom.

`Preview` itself does not replace `me.vdom` — `afterSetDockPreview` mutates `cn`, `applyTargetGeometry` mutates `cn[0].style` — so nothing in that class explains an id-less root. Which is the same wall as before, now with an address.

**Revised probe for AC-1:** capture the `{oldVnode.id, vnode.id, componentId}` triple **at the throw** together with its call site, rather than reading the component's vdom at boot. One stack frame separates `#L850` from `#L787`, and the two lead to different files. Reading `Preview` further cannot answer it.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-19T20:04:49Z

## AC-1 measured — it is the CHILD recursion, and both of my candidates were wrong

I instrumented the guard at `Helper.mjs:280` to carry its own stack, ran the file, reverted. Three hits, one distinct frame set:

```
Helper.createDeltas (Helper.mjs:280)
  <- Helper.createDeltas (Helper.mjs:323)
  <- Helper.update      (Helper.mjs:850)
  <- Helper.updateBatch (Helper.mjs:886)
  <- VDom.onRemoteMethod (RemoteMethodAccess.mjs:252)
```

So the throw is **one level below** the top-level pairing. `update()` at `:850` matched fine and recursed into the child loop; `:323` is the site. That is the call site [my previous note](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/18998#issuecomment-5744716025) ranked *"unlikely; children here are the affordance node, not the root"*, and it eliminates both candidates I had reasoned my way to — the vdom root never lost its id, and no moved-node insert is involved.

### The mechanism

The child loop matches a new child to an old child on one of two cases ([`Helper.mjs:311-316`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/vdom/Helper.mjs#L311)):

```js
// Case 1: Both nodes are elements with the same ID
(!childNode.componentId && !oldChildNode.componentId && childNode.id === oldChildNode.id) ||
// Case 2: Both nodes are placeholders for the same component
(childNode.componentId && childNode.componentId === oldChildNode.componentId)
```

**Case 2 matches on `componentId` alone and never looks at `id`** — and `createDeltas`' first act is to throw when the ids differ. So any two nodes carrying the same `componentId` but different identity satisfy the match and reach a guard that cannot accept them. The match and the guard disagree about what "the same node" means.

Our pair is exactly that: old `{id: neo-dock-preview-2, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}` is the Preview's own expanded root, new `{id: neo-vnode-806, cId: neo-dock-preview-2}` is a node of the same component that was never given an id, so `createVnode` generated one.

### Which makes the root defect the thing the loop's own comment claims cannot happen

Three lines above the match, `:308-310`:

> *"The VdomLifecycle mixin ensures that both the old (vnode) and new (vdom) trees are expanded to the same symmetric depth before diffing."*

They were not. At that child index the old tree holds the Preview's root and the new tree holds a node from inside it — an asymmetric expansion for this component. [`VdomLifecycle#createVdomReference`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs#L182) defines a placeholder as `{componentId}`, carrying an `id` *only* when the component designates a deeper node as its logical root — so for genuine placeholders the ids agree and Case 2's omission is harmless. It stops being harmless the moment an expanded node and an unexpanded one meet at the same index.

So there are two findings, and they need separating in the fix:

1. **Root** — the symmetric-depth invariant is violated for this component on this update. That is where the repair belongs.
2. **Proximate** — Case 2's predicate is wider than the comment above it, so the violation surfaces as a thrown error in the VDom worker instead of a re-key or a replace. A predicate that tests for *the presence of a structure* (`componentId`) rather than *the property that earns the match* (being the same node) is the same shape as [neomjs/neo-agent-brain#349](https://github.com/neomjs/neo-agent-brain/issues/349), settled earlier today on a different surface.

### One candidate falsified, before anyone spends a cycle on it

My first note floated giving `getAffordanceVdom`'s node a stable id (`${me.id}__affordance`). **That would not fix this.** A stable id changes `neo-vnode-806` into a predictable string; the pair would still be the component's root against a node inside it, still id-unequal, still thrown. It would have cost a cycle and moved nothing, which is why it stayed a note rather than a commit.

### Evidence

`dev@db3de7d7b5`, headless, `--workers=1`, `NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` wired. Probe applied to `Helper.mjs:280` only, run, and reverted — `git status` clean, no commit. Scene 4 and scene 5 still the only two reds; 8 passed, 3 skipped.

**AC-1 is met.** Next is AC-2: decide whether the repair lands on the expansion (root) or the predicate (proximate), with a red-first arm that fails on the unrepaired engine.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-19T20:34:39Z

## AC-2 — it is not dock-specific, and my last note read the direction backwards

Second probe: dumped the parent plus both child lists at every id-mismatched match, ran, reverted. Three hits, two distinct, both the same parent — `neo-dock-workspace-2`:

| idx | NEW tree | OLD tree |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `neo-container-29` · cId `neo-container-29` | `neo-container-29` · cId `neo-container-29` |
| 1 | **`neo-vnode-806`** · cId `neo-dock-preview-2` | **`neo-dock-preview-2`** · cId `neo-dock-preview-2` |
| 2 | **`neo-vnode-807`** · cId `neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicators-2` | **`neo-dashboard-dock-drop-indicators-2`** · cId same |

**Two children, not one.** `Preview` is not special — `DropIndicators` does the identical thing at the next index. Anything I concluded from reading `Preview` was reading the wrong subject.

### What the pattern actually is

In the NEW tree those two children are **unexpanded component references**; in the OLD tree they are the rendered nodes. [`VdomLifecycle#createVdomReference`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs#L182) returns `{componentId: me.id}` and attaches an `id` **only** when the component designates a deeper node as its logical root — so an ordinary child reference carries **no id at all**, and `createVnode` mints `neo-vnode-N` for it. It can never equal the rendered node's component-derived id.

Index 0 shows the contrast: `neo-container-29` is expanded on both sides, so its ids agree and it passes. **The trigger is a child list that mixes expanded and unexpanded children**, which is exactly what [`updateDepth`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs#L583) exists to produce: *"At Depth 1, these references are not expanded into the children's full VDOM trees."*

### So my previous note had the direction wrong

I wrote that Case 2 is *"wider than its own comment"*. It is not. **Case 2 exists precisely to pair an unexpanded reference with its rendered counterpart** — that is the only pair for which matching on `componentId` alone is the right test, because the reference has no id to match on. Case 2 is doing its job.

**It is the guard that does not know about the case Case 2 admits.** `createDeltas` opens by demanding `vnode.id === oldVnode.id`, which an unexpanded reference cannot satisfy by construction. The match and the guard were written against different models of the tree.

And the file already contains the shape of the answer, forty lines above, in [`compareAttributes`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/vdom/Helper.mjs#L51):

```js
// If either vnode is a component placeholder (indicated by the presence of componentId),
// we must not compare element attributes.
if (vnode.componentId || oldVnode.componentId) { return deltas }
```

One function short-circuits on placeholders; its caller throws on them.

### The fork, with falsifiers

| # | Repair | Falsifier |
|---|---|---|
| **1 (recommended)** | `createDeltas` short-circuits on an unexpanded reference, mirroring `compareAttributes`: the child owns its own update, so there is nothing to diff at this position | Fails if a delta is legitimately owed here — e.g. the child changed index and the move is emitted from this frame |
| 2 | Tighten Case 2 to require the reference shape on **both** sides, letting a mixed pair fall through to the remove/insert branch | Fails if that path destroys and recreates a live child component; a re-mount is far worse than the throw |
| 3 | Make the expansion symmetric upstream so a parent update never mixes expanded and unexpanded children | Fails if mixed expansion is intentional — and `updateDepth`'s own documentation says it is, which makes this option a contradiction of the feature rather than a repair of it |

I recommend **1**: it is the smallest change that makes the guard agree with the match, it has an in-file precedent in the same class, and it does not touch the scoped-update semantics. Option 3 reads as the "root cause" fix and I think that reading is a trap — the asymmetry is the feature.

**This is a core vdom diffing contract, not a dock leaf**, so I am putting the fork to peers before implementing rather than landing my own reading of it. The blast radius is every scoped update in the engine.

Probe applied to `Helper.mjs` only, run at `dev@db3de7d7b5`, reverted — `git status` clean, nothing committed.

### @neo-opus-grace - 2026-09-19T21:25:03Z

## Terminology note: `cId` is not a field

Raised by @tobiu, and he is right — the property is `componentId`.

`cId` is a label invented by the throw itself, [`Helper.mjs:280`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/db3de7d7b5/src/vdom/Helper.mjs#L280):

```js
throw new Error(`createDeltas() must be called for the same node. new: {id: ${vnode.id}, cId: ${vnode.componentId}}, old: {id: ${oldVnode.id}, cId: ${oldVnode.componentId}}`);
```

The value printed is `vnode.componentId`; `cId:` is literal text. `grep -rn '\bcId\b' src/` returns that one line and nothing else, so the abbreviation exists nowhere in the codebase as a real name. It reached this ticket because I quoted the error verbatim and never checked that its vocabulary matched the source's.

**Small defect worth carrying into the repair:** an error message that abbreviates a field to a name that does not exist costs every reader a grep that returns nothing — which is how it surfaced. The message should print `componentId`. One word, in the file this ticket is already changing.
